messages:
maya: Quick ask — we ran a regional GPU sweep for redwood-70b (q4f16) across H100/A100 variants. Posting the raw numbers below. Need a recommendation for per-GPU concurrency target + autoscale headroom for Dedicated clusters (us-east, eu-west, ap-sg). Also: has anyone seen p95s spike when using kernel_v2 during short bursts?

lucas: pasted results from the load runner:
```
Region | GPU  | kernel     | concurrency | qps  | p50(ms) | p95(ms)
us-east| H100 | kernel_v1  | 2           | 110  | 86      | 320
us-east| H100 | kernel_v2  | 2           | 95   | 72      | 180
eu-west| H100 | kernel_v1  | 2           | 100  | 92      | 340
ap-sg  | A100 | kernel_v1  | 2           | 60   | 120     | 450

us-east| H100 | kernel_v1  | 4           | 200  | 140     | 540
us-east| H100 | kernel_v2  | 4           | 170  | 110     | 290
```
Notes: kernel_v2 consistently lowers p95 but qps drops ~10-15% vs v1 at same concurrency. KV-cache warm starts improved p50 across the board (approx -10ms).

sophie: do we have burst sims (5–10 min) vs steady-state? my concern is that kernel_v2 seems to reduce tail when warmed, but under cold-warm transitions the p95 can spike because batching shapes change. would lean towards some headroom. :thinking_face:

aj: kernel_v2 uses a different fused attention kernel; better p95/p50 but less sustained throughput since it shards batched GEMMs differently. for Dedicated sizing i'd aim for concurrency target where p95 < 300ms for customer-facing routes. for H100 that looks like concurrency 3 is sweet spot from these numbers (interpolating between 2/4).

dmitri: suggested autoscale policy to avoid reactive overprovisioning: target ~70% avg GPU util, scale when sustained >80% for 60s, and keep a burst headroom of 25% (warm instances in reserve). warmup for new nodes = 90s. that should keep p95 under control during regional spikes.

lucas: quick cost/throughput note — kernel_v2 reduces tail but you pay in GPU-hours since qps per GPU falls. for eu-west we saw similar pattern but slightly worse network-limited throughput from the test infra. ap-sg on A100 is ~30% lower qps for same concurrency, so plan more GPUs or lower concurrency.

maya: summary proposal:
- H100 (us-east/eu-west): concurrency target = 3 per GPU; autoscale headroom = 25% (burst warm nodes)
- A100 (ap-sg): concurrency target = 2 per GPU; autoscale headroom = 30%
- Use kernel_v2 on p95-sensitive routes, kernel_v1 for max-cost-efficiency routes (batch-heavy)
- Run 1hr synthetic burst tests (5min spike every 10min) and collect 99/99.9 percentiles before finalizing proc.

maya: can someone update the capacity plan tracker and schedule the longer-run sim? linking doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/capacity/70b-regional-sweep (internal)

sophie: +1 on the 1hr sim. will run with continuous-batching on/off and capture KV-cache cold->warm transitions. i'll post results next week.

aj: i've queued a bench job with kernel_v2 @ concurrency 3 on us-east H100s — cmd i used: `bench-run --model redwood-70b --quant q4f16 --kernel kernel_v2 --gpu h100-us-east --concurrency 3 --duration 3600`

dmitri: adding autoscale rule draft to infra repo (PR incoming). i'll set warmup to 90s and reserve 25% capacity for bursts.

infra-bot: deploy-check: bench job queued (job-id: bj-48291) — notify when complete.

maya: perfect — thanks all. consensus: use concurrency=3 for H100s (us-east/eu-west), concurrency=2 for A100s (ap-sg), 25–30% headroom depending on region, prefer kernel_v2 for SLO-critical routes. i'll update the Dedicated sizing doc and loop in sales for pricing impact. :thumbsup:
